option_relations.rationale: The option describes a specific type of reactive arthritis post-COVID-19, which is not directly equivalent to 'Heberden nodes with seronegative arthritis'. While the vignette mentions COVID-19 and joint symptoms, the leaf focuses on Heberden nodes and seronegativity, which are not explicitly linked to 'Post-COVID-19 Reactive Arthritis' as an equivalent.

Osteoarthritis is a broader category of joint disease, and Heberden nodes are a classic manifestation of osteoarthritis, particularly at the DIP joints. Therefore, osteoarthritis is a supertype of 'Heberden nodes with seronegative arthritis', as Heberden nodes are a key feature of osteoarthritis.

Reactive arthritis (post-viral) is a type of arthritis that occurs after an infection. While the vignette mentions a viral infection (COVID-19) and joint symptoms, the leaf 'Heberden nodes with seronegative arthritis' does not directly equate to or imply reactive arthritis. Heberden nodes are more characteristic of osteoarthritis, not typically reactive arthritis.

Post-COVID-19 syndrome with osteoarticular and neurological manifestations describes a broader set of symptoms occurring after COVID-19. While the vignette mentions COVID-19 and joint symptoms, the leaf 'Heberden nodes with seronegative arthritis' is a specific finding that is not directly equivalent to or a subtype of this broad syndrome. The leaf focuses on specific joint findings (Heberden nodes) and seronegativity, which are not inherently part of the 'Post-COVID-19 syndrome' as defined in the option.
